chunks: Ibn Mahbub narrated from Hisham ibn Salim from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام about a mudabbar who intentionally killed a man. He said: “He is to be killed for him in retaliation.”

I said: “Then if he killed him by mistake?” He said: “He is handed over to the heirs of the slain, and he becomes their slave. If they wish, they may enslave him, and if they wish, they may sell him, but they have no right to kill him.”
Then he said: “O Abu Muhammad, indeed the mudabbar is owned property.”

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءِ ٱلْمَقْتُولِ: The heirs or legal claimants of the slain person
key_terms.مُدَبَّرٍ: A slave promised freedom upon the death of his master
key_terms.ٱسْتَرَقُّوا: They take him as a slave

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a mudabbar slave kills someone intentionally or by mistake?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a mudabbar, a slave whose freedom is deferred until the master’s death, if he kills someone. If the killing is intentional, qiṣāṣ applies; if it is accidental, he is handed over to the heirs of the victim as compensation, and they may keep or sell him but may not kill him. The Imam عليه السلام concludes by affirming that a mudabbar remains legally a slave.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5271 - Ibn Mahbub narrated from Hisham bin Salim from Abu Basir who said:

I asked Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) about a mudabbar (a slave promised freedom after the owner's death) who intentionally killed a man.
Imam (as) said: "He is to be killed in retaliation."

I asked: "What if he killed him by mistake?"
Imam (as) replied: "He is handed over to the heirs of the murdered person, and he becomes their slave. If they wish, they can enslave him, and if they wish, they can sell him, but they have no right to kill him."
Then Imam (as) said: "O' Abu Muhammad, indeed the mudabbar is still a slave."
